title: Selma Blair Apologizes for Plane Incident: ‘I Am So Sorry’
description: Selma Blair issued a video apology on Friday for the Oct. 11 incident in which she allegedly injured a flight attendant and kicked a nurse after be
body:
Selma Blair issued a video apology on Friday for the Oct. 11 incident in which she allegedly injured a flight attendant and kicked a nurse after being removed from a plane at John F. Kennedy International Airport.

	Blair, 54, is facing two state charges of 2nd-degree assault for the alleged attacks on the nurse and a Port Authority officer. 

	In a video posted to Instagram, the “Cruel Intentions” and “Legally Blonde” actress said she had been advised by her attorneys not to say much about the case.
	

	“What I can tell you, though, is very simple, and the truest thing I know about myself, and that not one day ever have I intended to hurt or frighten anyone a day in my life,” she said. “And so to the people that I disappointed, that I hurt, I frightened, alarmed: I am so sorry.”

	Blair’s reps have previously blamed a “medical emergency” for the episode aboard the flight from L.A. to New York.

	Blair was released from custody on $20,000 bail the following day. Blair’s attorney, Shawn Barnes, said in court that she had gotten on the flight after missing several doses of a drug that controls neurological symptoms. She also fell and hit her head during the flight.

	“These factors, your honor, coupled with the altitude, resulted in a state of severe confusion and disorientation,” Barnes said. “Ms. Blair did not get on that plane intending for any of this.”

	Blair is due back in court in Queens on Jan. 19.

schema.headline: Selma Blair Apologizes for Plane Incident: ‘I Am So Sorry’

title: Marvin R. Shanken, Longtime Publisher and Editor of Wine Spectator, Dies at 83
description: Marvin R. Shanken, the longtime editor and publisher of Wine Spectator magazine who was instrumental in elevating the profile of American wine busi
body:
Marvin R. Shanken, the longtime editor and publisher of Wine Spectator magazine who was instrumental in elevating the profile of American wine business, died Thursday in Manhattan. He was 83. 

	Shanken started his career in 1972 when he bought a small industry newsletter named Impact, which became a key resource for the wine and spirits industries. He purchased the struggling Wine Spectator newspaper in 1979, which he turned into a glossy magazine with more than 100,000 subscribers. 
	

	Wine Spectator became a key educational tool to help consumers become more familiar with the beverage, and contributed significantly to raising the status of the Napa Valley wine region. Wine Spectator articles utilized the 100 point wine rating system, which made buying fine bottles much more approachable for the general audience.

	Shanken also founded the magazine Cigar Aficionado and purchased Food Arts and Malt Advocate, which was renamed Whisky Advocate. Other publications he founded through his M. Shanken Communications include Market Watch and Shanken News Daily.   

	“He helped educate millions of Americans on the joys and virtues of wine, and tirelessly encouraged and pushed winemakers to produce the best for their customers,” Wine Spectator wrote in its obituary. 

	Among his many milestones were establishing Wine Spectator’s Restaurant Awards program, taking over the long-running Wine Experience weekend to bring producers together with consumers and creating the Wine Spectator Scholarship Foundation. 

	“It was an extremely influential publication that, along with Robert Parker, actually affected the way wine was made. Wine Spectator could make wineries halfway around the world change the way they made wine,” W. Blake Gray of the website Wine-Searcher told the New York Times. 
	

	Born in New Haven, Connecticut, Shanken studied business at the U. of Miami, then received an MBA from American U. in Washington. 

	He started off working in investment banking on Wall Street, during which time he was sent to California to help finance a vineyard purchase. This led to him developing a strong interest in wine and the industry. He pivoted his career to running the Impact newsletter, encouraged by its reception from alcoholic beverage wholesalers. At the time, there was very little substantial reporting on the wine business. 

	After he bought the struggling Wine Spectator newspaper, he relocated the offices from San Diego to San Francisco and became editor. The magazine expanded to cover travel, cooking, restaurants and collecting, and recently celebrated its 50th anniversary.  

	Shanken is survived by his wife, Hazel Rudy, daughters Jessica, Allison and Samantha, four grandchildren and two sisters.

schema.headline: Marvin R. Shanken, Longtime Publisher and Editor of Wine Spectator, Dies at 83

title: Cate Blanchett-Backed Group and Collection of Hollywood Stars File Brief in New York Times-OpenAI Lawsuit: Hollywood Has ‘Proven Infrastructure’ to License Content
description: The Human Consent Foundation, the Cate Blanchett-backed nonprofit trying to protect the likenesses of individuals from unauthorized scraping by AI
body:
The Human Consent Foundation, the Cate Blanchett-backed nonprofit trying to protect the likenesses of individuals from unauthorized scraping by AI models, and a legion of Hollywood companies have filed an amicus brief in the New York Times‘ lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft, claiming the tech companies’ position that it could not reasonably clear the rights for content “mischaracterizations” in light of an active licensing market. 
	

	The group’s 31-page brief was filed in the Southern District of New York late Friday, and the group was joined by CAA, the Music Artists Coalition, the National Association of Voice Actors, Writer, Inc, and the Creative Coalition on AI. The brief featured an appendix with a suite of Hollywood stars supportive of the cause, including Anne Hathaway, Emma Thompson, Dan Levy, Ron Howard, Madonna, Olivia Wilde and more


	“Defendants have argued that licensing creative works for AI training is cost-prohibitive,” the brief read. “Defendants also claim there is no settled means of valuing training data. The facts demonstrate otherwise. The creative industries already have in place a proven infrastructure and workflows to clear rights for dispersed works at scale and cost-effectively.”

	In a statement, HCF co-founder and CEO Nikki Hexum said the filing was intended to show the court “how the creative industry actually works and acknowledge the solutions that have been built and are continuing to develop for this new digital era.”

	“Our goal is to ensure that as the market for AI data licensing grows, the humans who create the value in that market are protected and have a meaningful choice,” Hexum added. “We are not starting from scratch. There is already a functioning market and infrastructure for licensing creative work. We just need to ensure that new AI technology respects those boundaries and choices, including the choice not to participate.”
	

	The brief came a day after SAG-AFTRA, the Writers Guild of America and the American Federation of Musicians filed their own brief against OpenAI and Microsoft, urging the court that the tech companies’ claim that their actions constituted fair use “would render moot the terms the unions and the industry agreed to at the bargaining table.”

	“It would harm not just the copyright owners, but the people who create the work,” their Thursday brief read.

	More to come…

schema.headline: Cate Blanchett-Backed Group and Collection of Hollywood Stars File Brief in New York Times-OpenAI Lawsuit: Hollywood Has ‘Proven Infrastructure’ to License Content

title: Magical Realist Tale ‘6TM’ and ‘Searching for SmarterChild,’ About One of the Earliest Chatbots, Win Top Industry Awards at Ji.hlava Festival
description: “6TM,” directed by Karim Akalay and produced by Walid Bekhti, won the New Visions Award for the most promising European project at the Ji.hlava Doc
body:
“6TM,” directed by Karim Akalay and produced by Walid Bekhti, won the New Visions Award for the most promising European project at the Ji.hlava Documentary Film Festival on Friday. The film is described as “a Belgian family comedy in three chapters, rooted in magic realism and the resilience of a community.”

	In the film, which is set over one scorching summer in the Cité Modèle, Brussels’ largest housing project, three stories unfold across one family. Two kids chase a magic lamp to keep their wheelchair-using friend from being forced out by broken elevators. A teenage girl builds a team of misfits for a soccer tournament. A mother rallies her neighbors to uncover who stole the rain.
	

	The jury said, “With its imaginative blend of magical realism, humor and social relevance, ‘6TM ‘ offers a fresh vision of European cinema. Rooted in lived experience and shaped through co-creation, ‘6TM’ challenges conventional representations and opens up new possibilities for who gets to tell stories, whose voices are heard, and who sees themselves reflected on screen. We believe this approach holds extraordinary promise for the next generation of both audiences and filmmakers, demonstrating how cinema can become more inclusive and participatory.”

	The jury was composed of Katrine Kiilgaard, managing director of CPH:DOX in Denmark; Anda Ionescu, managing partner and producer at Tangaj Production in Romania; and Robert Y. Chang, co-producer of American Documentary at POV in the U.S.

	The award was presented in cooperation with UPP, which donated an in-kind grant for visual post-production worth about 15,000 Euros, and Soundaquare, which provided sound mixing and a final sound master, with an estimated value of 5,000 Euros.
	

	The New Visions Award for the most promising U.S. project went to “Searching for SmarterChild,” directed by Lindsey Sitz and Zan Gillies, and produced by Erin Williams-Weir.

	The U.S.-Canadian film looks back to 2003, and the creation of SmarterChild, an online chatbot. He became a sounding board for a generation. People confided in him, insulted him and propositioned him.

	Twenty years later, as AI becomes deeply embedded in our lives, what does our treatment of the first internet chatbot say about us? By revisiting our cringe-worthy conversations, the film explores the darkest parts of human nature, accountability, and what it takes to change, not only the technologies we create, but ourselves.

	The jury said, ” ‘Searching for SmarterChild’ takes us back to the early days of the internet to confront one of the most pressing questions of our time: what does our relationship with artificial intelligence reveal about ourselves? By revisiting their interactions with one of the earliest chatbots of their childhoods, the filmmakers offer a perspective on today’s fascination with AI, challenging us to reflect not only on the technologies we create, but also on how we treat them and each other. The jury wishes to recognize the project’s promise to engage audiences through an original, entertaining and thought-provoking approach to a subject that will profoundly shape our collective future.”

	The award was presented in partnership with AmDocs, with the winner receiving $7,000 in cash.

	The festival also accorded the APA World Excellence Award to renowned Danish producer Signe Byrge Sørensen. The award honors her “outstanding contribution to international film production and her remarkable achievements in world cinema.”

title: Trinh T. Minh-ha Still Sets Her Own Rules – and Heads to ‘The Undying Desert’ in Her First Film Set in the U.S. (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Vietnamese-American filmmaker, writer, feminist and post-colonial theorist Trinh T. Minh-ha is readying her upcoming film “The Undying Desert.”

	“
body:
Vietnamese-American filmmaker, writer, feminist and post-colonial theorist Trinh T. Minh-ha is readying her upcoming film “The Undying Desert.”

	“I’ve just finished editing it,” she told Variety at Ji.hlava Documentary Film Festival, where she’s celebrating a retrospective.

	“I’ve made films in Africa, China, Vietnam and Japan, and people would ask: ‘When are you going to make a film about the U.S.?’ They were right, because I live there.”
	

	She has been shooting in the Great Basin Desert for almost two decades.

	“A desert is huge, majestic and beautiful. At the same time, it’s considered ‘arid’ by colonizing forces. All these prejudices about what a desert is still exist in our language. But it’s actually very lively,” she stated.

	In “The Undying Desert,” she examines people’s relationship with it.

	“For me, this film is closely related to the way of life of indigenous people, especially Native Americans. The other theme has to do with why we go to the desert in the first place. It wipes away every notion that allows us to conform to certain ways of life. Suddenly, you don’t have to be polite or compete with others. You go there to be with your true self.”

	Not everyone is ready for that, though.

	“Some just use it as a terrain for sports. They’re there, but they are not with the desert. Native Americans see the desert as layers and layers of life, but it’s even more radical. They always remember that their ancestors are with them too. Life and death go together.”

	Trinh T. Minh-ha is not finished with this subject just yet – she started working on another film immediately after “The Undying Desert.” Co-directed with longtime collaborator Jean-Paul Bourdieu, it will also be set there.
	

	“In the Great Basin Desert, there are groups of people who isolate themselves and turn this location into a research center for Mars. They plan to go there and colonize another planet,” she said.

	“With every one of these trips to the desert, I could see myself changing. I was learning how I feel and what the desert actually brings me.”

	With works such as “Forgetting Vietnam,” “Surname Viet Given Name Nam,” “Reassemblage” and “What About China?,” she never focuses on individual stories.

	“It’s like poetry, where the ‘I’ is collective. You’re inviting people to come in,” she explained.

	“I’ve always been engaged in politics, but as Jean-Luc Godard also noticed, there’s a difference between the political and politics. Everything we do can be political. This is particularly relevant for women because we’re very attuned to everyday activities. If you remain blind to that, you might make a political film about a progressive subject. But the way you treat it can be very regressive. When you turn the camera toward someone else, you also have to turn it toward yourself.”

	For Trinh T. Minh-ha, “cinema is not just an experience for the eyes.”

	“It’s an experience for the whole body. When I was first showing ‘Reassemblage,’ someone told me: ‘I’m hearing this film with my eyes and seeing it with my ears.’ I replied: ‘Perfect’,” she smiled.

	“In East Asia, the senses are not that separate. They overlap. A painter is also a musician and a poet. I think it’s the same with film. It’s better to come with an open mind and see how it speaks to you, rather than focusing on what constitutes a ‘good documentary,’ or what its story or message is.”

	That’s what she tells emerging filmmakers, too.

	“You set up the rules for yourself. I’m very glad that I was able to stick with the path I chose and not be intimidated by all these oppressive regulations.”

	Documentary filmmakers have more leeway today, she argued. But that doesn’t mean one should take all this freedom for granted.

	“On the contrary, you have to be much more responsible because you are the one setting the rules. When people ask if your film is fiction or documentary, you have to find a way to talk to them. And say: ‘Why do you need to know?’ Of course, you don’t always succeed. Even after so many years of making films, producers or programmers are not immediately interested in my work. But I’m still building my audience.”

schema.headline: Trinh T. Minh-ha Still Sets Her Own Rules – and Heads to ‘The Undying Desert’ in Her First Film Set in the U.S. (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘The Celebrity Traitors’: [SPOILER] and [SPOILER] Win in Nail-Biting Season 2 Finale
description: SPOILER ALERT: This post contains spoilers for the finale episode of the U.K. version of “The Celebrity Traitors” Season 2, now streaming on BBC iP
body:
SPOILER ALERT: This post contains spoilers for the finale episode of the U.K. version of “The Celebrity Traitors” Season 2, now streaming on BBC iPlayer.

	It was the feel-good ending hardly anyone expected: “The Traitors” season finale resulted in an unexpected win by Faithfuls Sebastian Croft and Romesh Ranganathan, as both Traitors King Kenny and Maya Jama were banished from the game during a tense showdown.


	It was also an outcome unthinkable only a day prior. James Acaster’s admission at the roundtable that he had been a secretly recruited Traitor put an end to a seemingly unstoppable Traitors run. Traitor Maya Jama then fell on her sword not long after murdered Faithful Michael Sheen had worked it out.
	

	Yet, the ending wasn’t entirely a happy one. James Blunt, who had been adamant about who was a Traitor, was evicted, even though he had been Faithful. His confident, yet not entirely accurate predictions at the roundtable, were perhaps his biggest downfall.


	Despite the unlikely twist of the Faithfuls winning here, though, the first season of “The Celebrity Traitors” was the definition of a tough act to follow. Alan Carr’s journey from the worst Traitor imaginable to somehow fooling everyone and claiming victory is arguably the greatest moment the U.K. franchise has ever had, in a season that will otherwise forever be remembered for Faithful Celia Imrie’s fart.

	This season, Richard E. Grant admitting he was a Traitor mere moments after being picked as a Traitor was on par with Alan’s time in the turret (“You need to make it very clear that you’re not,” responded confused Faithful James Blunt), but his admission and eventual departure set off a chain of events that this season found harder to recover from.
	

	Acaster, who had said from the start that he did not want to be a Traitor, had to reluctantly accept the offer by Grant and Maya Jama to become one to avoid being murdered. The show is always in its element when the Traitors go on a gleeful killing spree at night while lying to the Faithfuls during the day, but Acaster’s understandable reluctance and difficulty in getting stuck in meant the dynamic that the show thrives on never got going.

	It was made worse by the fact that another chain of events meant that Professor Hannah Fry’s later recruitment as a Traitor couldn’t get into gear either. As game rules meant it was only her and Jerry Hall up for murder the same night, recruitment was not the only option. Viewers would have been disappointed if she had been chosen to leave, but with little room for maneuver she ran out of road.

	Thankfully, “The Traitors” on a bad day is still better than most reality shows on a good one. There’s still a camp absurdity, albeit a little less than a usual series, which makes the more tense moments easier to stomach if reality television is not your bag. The parts when “The Traitors” flies highest are moments that the producers can’t even predict. For example, Ross Kemp might be able to interview a cartel boss in the Amazon rainforest, but he could not handle being brushed on the arm by Leigh-Anne Pinnock from Little Mix.

	An underwhelming season, and this rather underwhelming conclusion, will not unravel “The Traitors” either. The format of the show is flexible enough in that no season feels like a repeat of the last one. Even older reality shows when they were firmly in their prime, like “Big Brother” on Channel 4, had the odd season where the ingredients were there but stars never truly aligned. The BBC couldn’t be prouder of the ratings this season received — an unbelievable 15 million viewers, a number British television usually only gets for a royal wedding or an international football finals.

	Yet perhaps this season of “The Celebrity Traitors” exposed the show’s natural limitations. But it’s something that can be fixed. It seems that if you don’t want to be a Traitor and you are picked to be a Traitor, it is harder for the show to fly. The early banishments of Grant and Fry also made more obvious a flaw dedicated fans had been pointing out for a while: you might as well keep an obvious Traitor in the game early in the show, because if you kick them out they will be replaced by another Traitor anyway.
	

	And for all of the comedy that Richard E. Grant provided for such a short time in the opening episodes, keeping him in the castle for longer was likely what the producers wanted anyway.

schema.headline: ‘The Celebrity Traitors’: [SPOILER] and [SPOILER] Win in Nail-Biting Season 2 Finale

title: Music Industry Moves: Chris Young Signs With UTA; Kurt Vile Re-Ups With Third Side Publishing
description:
Grammy-nominated singer-songwriter and Grand Ole Opry member Chris Young has signed with UTA for global representation in all areas.

	The signing
body:
Grammy-nominated singer-songwriter and Grand Ole Opry member Chris Young has signed with UTA for global representation in all areas.

	The signing comes as Young approaches nearly two decades in the country music spotlight. In addition to his robust solo catalog, over the years he has performed with Miranda Lambert, Jon Pardi, Ashley McBryde and others.

	“I’m very excited to move into this new chapter at UTA. I really feel like there is a plan and a vision for growth and moving forward,” Young said.
	

	UTA Agent Brian Hill added, “Chris is a world-class singer, songwriter, and live performer. We’re excited to welcome him to the UTA family, and we look forward to building upon the incredible foundation he’s already established. This is only the beginning!”

	+ Kurt Vile has inked a new long-term co-publishing deal with Third Side Music, which expands the independent global music publisher’s representation to the Philadelphia rocker’s Vile’s entire catalog, including his solo material and works by Kurt Vile and the Violators. TSM will also administer his future works beginning with his latest album, “Philadelphia’s Been Good to Me.”

	“Kurt is one of the real ones. An incredible singer-songwriter who can turn seemingly effortless phrases into deep in your head hooks, all backed by low-key trips to shredsville. All around good dude. Back in 2015, we started working together on the release of B’lieve I’m Goin Down…, and I’m stoked to now include the prior back catalog into the work, and also be in the long-term KV business. We grindin’,” says Jeff Waye, COO and co-founder of TSM.
	

	+ WME has hired two new agents for its contemporary music team: Aleks Ljubojevic and Sophia Simon. The announcement was made by Kirk Sommer, Global Head of Music at WME.

	Ljubojevic will bring electronic artist and producer and Swedish House Mafia member Steve Angello with him to WME for representation in Europe for his solo career. He joins WME from Ace Agency in Amsterdam, where he represented Martin Garrix, Sam Feldt, Don Diablo, and many others in the electronic music space. He will focus on expanding WME’s electronic music roster and driving growth opportunities for both emerging and established talent. Ljubojevic is based in London and reports to Stephanie LaFera, Partner and Head of EMD at WME.

	Simon joins WME from So.Connected, the agency she founded in 2024 focused on developing international artists and music projects in the Brazilian market. Through the agency, she has worked with artists and labels including Martin Garrix, NE-YO, Jason Mraz, Ultra Records, Maddix, Sean Paul, Alesso, and Soulja Boy, and has helped develop BRESH’s presence in Brazil. She previously co-managed Brazilian singer-songwriter and actress Giulia Be and worked as a day-to-day manager at Milk & Honey. Simon is based in Spain and reports to Rob Markus, Senior Partner and Head of International at WME.

	“Aleks and Sophia both have strong track records of developing talent, building international touring businesses, and creating opportunities for artists across key markets worldwide,” said Sommer. “The future of music is global, and their additions to our team continue to strengthen WME’s position as the leading agency for long-term global success.”

	+ Rothenberg, Mohr & Binder LLP has announced the promotion of Joseph Duthie to Partner. Duthie’s promotion comes as RMB continues to invest across its New York and Beverly Hills offices.

	Duthie, who joined RMB in 2021 and is based in the firm’s New York office, works closely with Gunna, Lisa, Marshmello, Jon Bellion, Charlie Puth and TDE Top Dawg Entertainment. His roster includes Matt Maschi and Louis Coppola’s new record/publishing venture Lavoro Media Group, recording artist and producer Kurtis Wells, recording artist Harvey Brittain and producer Hamish.

	Founding Partners Paul Rothenberg, Jeremy Mohr and Josh Binder said jointly: “We are excited to welcome Joe to our partnership. Joe is a tireless attorney with an instinct for the deal. Beyond first-rate legal work, he has invested himself in the operations and growth of our New York office. We look forward to more success alongside him and the incredible group of partners, associates, and colleagues at RMB.”
	

	+ Veteran concert promoter Jason Legassie has announced the launch of Off the Rails Presents, a Massachusetts-based independent concert promoter with national reach. The new firm will present music and more at venues including Off the Rails in Worcester, MA 01608) and the new Off The Rails Boston. Legassie will serve as vice president and operating partner alongside co-founder Chris Besaw, who will operate the Boston venue.

	“I am thrilled for this latest challenge in my career and eager to build OTR Presents from the ground up into something truly special,” says Legassie. “OTR Presents is open for business, not just in the Northeast but nationwide.”

	+ Warner Chappell Music, the global music publishing arm of Warner Music Group, has signed an administration and sub-publishing deal with Satori Song, the publishing company of French pop singer-songwriter Étienne Daho.

	The agreement, which was orchestrated by WCM France’s President Matthieu Tessier and A&R Director Jérôme Brucker, covers Daho’s entire 45-year discography, from his 1981 debut album, “Mythomane,” to his latest release, “Tirer la nuit sur les étoiles.” The deal encompasses more than 200 songs, including his celebrated works written and composed for Vanessa Paradis, Jane Birkin, Françoise Hardy, Dani, and Marianne Faithfull.

	“I’m delighted to be joining the Warner Chappell Music France roster as I embark on an exciting new chapter in my career,” Daho said.

	Tessier added, “Working alongside a great artist like Étienne Daho and helping champion his repertoire, both in France and internationally, is a great privilege for all of us at Warner Chappell Music. I would like to extend my deepest thanks to Étienne and his producer Laurent Manganas for their trust.”

	+ Management company Neon Coast has promoted Nikki Boon to Chief Creative Officer. She has been with the company for a decade, working closely country star Kane Brown and global independent alt-pop band Nightly. In her new role, will provide creative oversight and direction for every artist at Neon Coast as well as international strategy

	“Nikki’s creative thinking is second to none. She has a passion for our artists that you can feel in every conversation she has,” said Martha Earls, Founder and Owner of Neon Coast.
	

	+ Peermusic has completed its acquisition of Australia-based 120 Publishing as announced by the company’s Mary Megan Peer and Ralph W. Peer. In connection with the transaction, Peermusic has appointed 120 Publishing General Manager, Karen Hamilton, as Managing Director, Peermusic Australasia.

	The deal will give Peermusic the publishing rights to 120 Publishing’s approximately 5,000 works and 120,000 administered copyrights. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed.

	Mary Megan Peer noted: “The acquisition of 120 Publishing marks our continued investment in the Australasian market and repertoire. We are proud to steward a catalog with such artistic talent and cultural importance, ensuring these songs and songwriters continue to find new opportunities globally.”

	+ Former Universal Music Group exec Cristina Pimentel and former Andreessen Horowitz partner Caitlin Glazebrook have launched Duets Network, Inc. to help startups in sports, entertainment and the creator economy. The company’s goal is to be a one-stop shop for founders, bringing investor connections, expert guidance and business resources together on a single online platform. It was recently showcased at LA and SF Tech Weeks.

	Pimentel said, “At Universal Music Group, I kept meeting founders with promising businesses who didn’t know where to turn for help. Finding someone who understands your industry and the problem you’re trying to solve, early on, can make a real difference. Caitlin and I are building Duets with this community to make those connections easier than ever.”

	Glazebrook added, “When I was at Andreessen Horowitz, I spent a lot of time fielding pitches from startups that weren’t right for our fund. Angels and emerging fund managers face the same challenge with far less bandwidth. We’re building Duets as an extension of their teams, helping them source and vet startups that fit their investment criteria.”

	Monday, Oct. 26

	Mary J. Blige has sold undisclosed shares of her publishing and recorded-music assets to Primary Wave Music, the company announced on Monday morning. Included in the deal are some of Blige’s greatest hits, including “Family Affair,’ “My Life,” “Mary Jane (All Night Long),” “You Bring Me Joy,” “Be Without You,” “I Can Love You,” and others; further details were not announced. 
	

	Known universally as “the Queen of Hip-Hop Soul,” over the course of her three-decade-plus career Blige has sold an estimated 50 million records worldwide across 15 studio albums, two live albums and 83 singles, which have garnered her nine Grammy Awards amid 37 Grammy nominations, two Oscar and one Emmy nom. She was honored with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 2018 and inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2024. She kicked off her first-ever Las Vegas residency, “Mary J. Blige: My Life, My Story.” The 20-date residency began this past May and will run through February 2027 at Dolby Live at Park MGM.

	Natalia Nastaskin, Primary Wave’s Chief Content Officer, said “From the moment I heard ‘You Remind Me’ on NY’s KISS-FM, I became a Day 1 Mary J. Blige fan. For over 30 years, she has gifted the world with hit after undeniable hit and in the process has created the soundtrack of our lives. To partner with the Queen herself on her extraordinary catalog and her everlasting legacy is an honor for me and for our entire Primary Wave team.”

	* Sandlot-Atlantic Outpost recording artist Stella Lefty, who is enjoying one of the biggest hits of the year with “Boston,” has signed with Nashville-based Make Wake Artists for management representation. At the company, which also manages Luke Combs, Lefty will be managed by founder and CNO (Chief Navigation Officer) Chris Kappy and managing partner Sophia Sansone.

	Launched in 2015, the company’s roster includes Jon Bellion, Flatland Cavalry, and Dylan Marlowe, among others.

	“Stella’s connection to her fans reminds me of Luke’s fan connection very early on… It is real!!!,” Kappy said in a statement. “Stella has the talent, authenticity and drive to build something truly special, and our team is committed to helping her realize that potential.”

	+ Veteran vocal group Boyz II Men have signed with Warner Records Nashville and will launch an all-new country project, scheduled for release in 2027. Since emerging from Philadelphia with their 1991 debut, “Cooleyhighharmony,” the group has sold an estimated 60 million albums worldwide and wont four Grammy Awards and a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.

	“Boyz II Men’s global influence is decades in the making,” shared Warner Records Nashville Chair & President, Cris Lacy. “Every genre and culture has benefited from their original music, and their impact on artists in the current country landscape, while perhaps surprising to some, is quite profound. When I learned that growing up listening to artists like Randy Travis was seminal in their desire to collaborate with Nashville’s award-winning singers and songwriters, I knew we had to be a part of it.”
	

	+ Pop vet JoJo has partnered with Seeker Music, which has acquired the singer-songwriter’s original and re-recorded versions of her first two albums – “JoJo” and “The High Road” – as well as future releases and projects. The celebration kicks off with Seeker’s release of a deluxe 20th anniversary edition of “The High Road,” featuring the original album and four bonus tracks from the original 2006 editions, as well as acoustic versions. Jojo has also collaborated in the past with Seeker CEO and founder Evan Bogart; Seeker already held interest in two of her hits via deals with other cowriters.

	“Deciding who to trust with such a personal and important part of my catalog wasn’t something I took lightly,” Jojo said. “Over time it was heartening to learn more about Seeker’s ethos and see how involved and passionate Evan is — someone who truly understands artists because he is a creator himself. It feels full-circle to have both versions of these albums together with a team committed to finding new ways to amplify it.”

	Bogart added, “I’ve personally been such a fan for so long, and it means the world to all of us at Seeker to be partnering with her. This is just the beginning!”

	+ Believe has named Mel Curley as Global Head of Editorial & Marketing Partnerships. Based in New York, Mel will report to Darya Pourshasb, Believe’s Chief Marketing Officer. According to the announcement, Curley will lead Believe’s global EMP strategy, strengthening relationships with key digital platforms and unlocking new editorial and promotional opportunities to support artists and labels growth and international development across Believe’s Artist Services, Label & Artist Solutions and TuneCore.

	She joins from Amazon Music, where she served as Global Head of Independent Label Relations, overseeing relationships with more than 350 independent distributors, labels and artists. Previously, she held senior positions at Arista Records and at Sony Music Entertainment.

	Pourshasb said, “As competition for audience attention intensifies, our ability to connect artists and labels with fans across digital platforms has never been more important, which is why Editorial and Marketing Partnerships are a key pillar of our music marketing strategy. Mel brings an exceptional combination of DSP expertise, music industry experience and strategic vision.”
	

	+ Hybe Americas has announced the launch of Tru Records, a new record label “created to discover and develop the next generation of Latin pop artists,” according to the announcement. Latin music veteran Alejandro Mejía will be the company’s first general manager, and its first artist is Santos Bravos, the first Latin pop group created by Hybe Americas.

	“The launch of Tru Records represents a unique opportunity to champion Latin American talent and bring it to new audiences around the world,” Mejía said. “Starting this new chapter with Santos Bravos and with the support of Hybe Americas allows us to build careers with international reach while staying true to our Latin identity and the stories we tell.”

title: ‘Obsession’ Director Curry Barker Pitched Nathan Fielder a Collaboration After Watching ‘You Can See Everything’: ‘I Put It Out in the Water’
description: “Obsession” director Curry Barker is not only a fan of “You Can See Everything,” but he’s already reached out to Nathan Fielder about working toget
body:
“Obsession” director Curry Barker is not only a fan of “You Can See Everything,” but he’s already reached out to Nathan Fielder about working together.

	“I thought it was freakin’ insane and awesome,” Barker told Variety Thursday night at the Time100 Next Gala at Pier59 Studios . “I didn’t know much about [Elizabeth Holmes’] story going into it. I feel like I missed certain tiny things, but it was three hours long and I wished it was longer. That’s rare, you know?”
	

	When asked about potentially collaborating with Fielder, the “Obsession” director revealed he’s already floated the idea to him: “I told him that. I said, ‘Hey!’ … I just put it out in the water.”

	“You Can See Everything” blurs the line between narrative and documentary storytelling and, as Variety’s chief awards editor Clayton Davis puts it, has “turned the movie landscape topsy-turvy.” Much like Barker’s “Obsession,” the film has left the industry re-examining what kinds of movies resonate with Gen Z audiences — and, more importantly, what drives them out to the theaters.

	“It felt new, fresh, different,” Barker said of “You Can See Everything.” “You almost can’t even call it a documentary, but it totally is. I’m just a huge fan of what [Fielder] is doing.”

	Barker should have plenty more chances to cross paths with Fielder on the awards circuit, as both their films continue to earn recognition alongside some of the year’s most acclaimed films.

	“The events are really cool,” Barker said. “I did the Academy Gala and I was just blown away. I mean, every direction you look is someone that you’ve seen your entire life on social media, and you’re like, ‘Holy cow, this person’s here. This person’s here.’ That was a crazy experience.”
	

	But one celebrity encounter in particular left Barker starstruck: Emma Watson.

	“I was a huge ‘Harry Potter’ fan growing up, and I saw Emma Watson and I froze,” Barker recalled. “It’s so weird, I’m meeting all of these people that I really look up to, but there’s something different about when it’s someone from your childhood that really means a lot. That changes where you’re like, ‘Oh, woah.’ I was totally weird to her. I was trying to play it cool. But I did not play it cool.”

	Barker was honored alongside Raye, Druski, Paapa Essiedu and several other Hollywood rising stars at Time100 Next. The night kicked off with an intimate performance from Raye, who performed a jazzy rendition of “Cry Me a River” and “Happier Times Ahead.” Himesh Patel, Alex Warren and several other nominees made toasts throughout the night, but Ashley Padilla of “Saturday Night Live” fame got the biggest reaction from the crowd.“It’s hard to give a toast when you believe you should not be here,” the comedian quipped. “I was going to say something like the children when they asked me who or what gives me hope for the future. But I realized I don’t know any. I know my niece and nephew. and one of them called me a bitch last week. I’m not gonna say which… my niece! My nephew’s an angel. But I’m not gonna hang all my hope on those guys!”Next up for Barker is “Anything But Ghosts,” set for release on May 7, 2027. Seth Rogen, who penned Barker’s Time100 Next profile, already saw the film — and claims that Barker’s sophomore feature is “even better” than “Obsession.”

	“I’ve seen Curry’s next film, ‘Anything But Ghosts’ — and for those of you who, like me, are uncomfortable with this amount of talent in a person so young, I have bad news … it’s even better,” Rogen wrote. “And, to add insult to injury, he’s just as good an actor as he is a director.”

schema.headline: ‘Obsession’ Director Curry Barker Pitched Nathan Fielder a Collaboration After Watching ‘You Can See Everything’: ‘I Put It Out in the Water’

title: Netflix’s ‘Cliff Booth’ Won’t Play in Regal and Cinemark Imax Theaters
description: Netflix’s push to release more films on the big screen hasn’t come without a few hiccups. Most recently, theater chains including Regal Cinemas are
body:
Netflix’s push to release more films on the big screen hasn’t come without a few hiccups. Most recently, theater chains including Regal Cinemas are declining to play the streaming platform’s “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” on their Imax screens. Cinemark also turned down the “Cliff Booth” booking, according to sources.

	“Cliff Booth,” which stars Brad Pitt and is directed by David Fincher, is still set to play on AMC’s Imax screens for a two-week release beginning Nov. 25 before releasing on the streaming platform Dec. 23.
	

	News of the release plans was first reported by Puck. 

	Lionsgate’s “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” is currently set to occupy a majority of cinemas with its upcoming Nov. 20 premiere. The exhibitors would have had to give up some of their “Hunger Games” Imax screens for “Cliff Booth,” which streams just a month later — a no-go for some circuits.

	With AMC’s 200 Imax screens available in the U.S. and several others offered internationally by independent cinemas, “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” will play on more than 500 screens worldwide. Regal has approximately 100 Imax screens and Cinemark around 20, while some other smaller chains will reportedly not book “Cliff Booth” either. 

	Fincher’s film is one of several upcoming Netflix titles slated for a theatrical release, including “Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew,” which will see a wide release (including Imax screens) for almost 50 days, “The Mosquito Bowl,” “Ray Gunn” and “Charlie vs. the Chocolate Factory.” The streaming platform reported grosses for the first time for the big-screen debut earlier this month of “La Bola Negra,” which brought in over $277,000 across just four theaters and marked the second-highest screen average for a non-English language film behind 2019’s “Parasite.”

title: Hotel and Travel Industry Groups Back U.S. Film Incentive as Tourism Draw
description: Lobbying groups representing the hotel and travel industries have endorsed a 20% federal tax incentive for film and TV production, arguing that dom
body:
Lobbying groups representing the hotel and travel industries have endorsed a 20% federal tax incentive for film and TV production, arguing that domestic filming attracts tourism from abroad.

	The American Hotel & Lodging Association and the U.S. Travel Association have joined an alliance of film industry stakeholders in pushing for the bill. The two groups represent airlines, ticketing sites, hotel companies and resorts, including the Disney and Universal theme parks.
	

	“Every film and TV production made in America sends a ripple through the travel economy, filling hotel rooms, restaurants and small businesses during the shoot and inspiring travelers to visit long after the credits roll,” said Geoff Freeman, president and CEO of the U.S. Travel Association, in a statement. “A federal production incentive would bring that economic activity back to communities in all 50 states and give destinations of every size a powerful new way to showcase themselves to the world.”

	A bipartisan group of lawmakers introduced the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act last month. The bill would create a 20% tax credit for labor on film and TV productions in the U.S., with 5% bonuses for independent film and for filming in rural areas and disaster zones.

	The bill now has 52 sponsors in the House of Representatives and 10 sponsors in the Senate. The House sponsors are heavily concentrated in filming states, with 15 from California, six from Pennsylvania, four from New York, and three each from New Jersey, Illinois and Georgia.

	The House bill has been referred to the Ways and Means Committee, which handles tax legislation, while the Senate version is in the Finance Committee. Supporters are hoping to pass the bill during the lame duck session that begins a week after the midterm election.
	

	“The economic benefits of this measure extend well beyond the film and television industry,” said Ralph Posner, spokesman for the American Hotel & Lodging Association. “Domestic production brings cast, crew, and suppliers into communities across the U.S., bolstering hotel demand and supporting local businesses. By encouraging more domestic production activity, the legislation will help drive economic growth, support local communities, and showcase U.S. destinations to audiences around the world.”

	Backers of the bill also include the Motion Picture Association, which represents the major studios, as well as the Independent Film and Television Alliance all of the Hollywood unions.

schema.headline: Hotel and Travel Industry Groups Back U.S. Film Incentive as Tourism Draw

body:
Bill Belichick & Jordon Hudson
                          Secretly Split Last Year
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 30, 2026
                            3:48 PM PDT
                                                                            
              
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Bill Belichick and Jordon Hudson called it quits late last year, and there's already been another person in the picture ... TMZ Sports has learned.
      
    
            Sources close to Jordon, with direct knowledge, tell TMZ ... the legendary football coach, now for the University of North Carolina, and his much younger girlfriend quietly ended their romance "late last year."
      
    
            Although, they're no longer dating, we're told they remain "committed to their business partnerships and remain close friends."
      
    
            It's unclear what led to Jordon and Bill's breakup, or who ultimately pulled the plug on their romance.
      
    
            Another source tells us Jordon has started seeing other people, but we don't know what her relationship status is right now.
      

            We've reached out to Bill and Jordon ... so far, no word back.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Publicly, neither Bill or Jordon let on about their breakup. They've appeared together at events all year, and just last week, Jordon was on the sidelines, supporting Bill at UNC's home game against Syracuse.
      
    
            TMZ Sports broke the story ... Bill, 74, and Jordon, 25, met on a flight in February 2021 and began dating in 2022, though their romance didn't go public until June 2024.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Their nearly 50-year age gap raised eyebrows, but the couple appeared unfazed by the attention.
      
    
            Jordon sparked controversy in April 2025 after interrupting Bill's CBS "Sunday Morning" interview when he was asked how they met. Bill later defended her, claiming the interview was edited to create a false narrative.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            More recently, Bill dismissed claims Jordon was trying to control UNC's football program, calling the accusations ridiculous in a September interview with the Wall Street Journal.

title: Christa Pike Demands End to Solitary Confinement After Botched Execution
description:
Christa Pike
                          I Survived Death, Now I'm Suffering All Alone!!!
body:
Christa Pike
                          I Survived Death, Now I'm Suffering All Alone!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 30, 2026
                            2:03 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  October 30, 2026
                                3:46 PM PDT
                                    
              
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Christa Pike survived a botched execution ... but now she's fighting another battle behind bars, asking a federal judge to get her out of solitary confinement ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            According to court documents, obtained by TMZ, Pike filed an emergency motion Friday, claiming Tennessee prison officials are violating a 2024 settlement agreement that was supposed to end her decades-long isolation.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Pike's attorneys say she's been kept alone in the prison infirmary since returning from the hospital Oct. 9 ... with officials refusing to say when she'll be allowed to interact with other inmates again.
      

            The docs say the settlement previously allowed Pike to work, eat meals, exercise, and socialize with other women in custody ... privileges her legal team says have now been stripped away.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Pike claims the isolation is taking a serious psychological toll ... especially after spending 28 years in solitary confinement before reaching the agreement ... saying in a sworn declaration each day she's kept alone only makes things worse.
      
    
            And she's raising concerns about her living conditions, too ... claiming she's been forced to clean a roach-infested shower herself, despite suffering severe burns, nerve damage, and painful wounds from the failed execution.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Her attorneys, Angie Bergman, Brian Roark and Hannah Webber, tell TMZ the state has ignored repeated warnings that Pike's isolation violates their agreement ... prompting them to seek emergency court intervention.
      
    
            Pike is asking to be housed alongside other women receiving medical care, where she says she could safely recover without being completely cut off from fellow inmates.
      
    
            She also requests the judge to fast-track the case ... proposing a Nov. 4 deadline for the state's response.
      
    
            As TMZ previously reported ... Pike survived Tennessee's Sept. 30 execution attempt despite receiving two doses of a lethal injection drug. She spent days on a ventilator and more than a week in intensive care.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The 50-year-old remains on death row for the 1995 murder of Colleen Slemmer ... and Tennessee's governor has indicated he expects her death sentence will remain in place unless a court decides otherwise.
